chapter: Dancers, Newton, Chu Berry and the Cab Calloway band
title: How 'Ratamacue', 'Paradiddle' and 'Crescendo' came about
summary: Rudiments practiced at the Cotton Club became arranged features.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: '61, right. Why don't we just run down--one thing about Dizzy is that Dizzy arranged "Paradiddle".
Let's talk about those things. There were three things that you did with that band that were features for you and one was "Paradiddle" and the other two were "Ratamacue" and "Crescendo on Drums"
And Dizzy made the arrangement on "Paradiddle". Walter Thomas made the arrangement on "Ratamacue."
Walter made that arrangement for Cab's band.
"Ratamacue" is recorded with your first session with that band.
In 1939. How did that come about?

Well in between sets. See there at the Cotton Club, I used to go upstairs and practice on my practice pad. And we used to practice a lot of rudiments. In which the rudiments is drumming as ratamacue, paradiddle, Flam, Double stroke roll, Single stroke roll, etc. So I was upstairs practicing this ratamacue.
A ratamacue, it's a beat, it's a drag, it's like ba da da da da, ba da da da da (DRUMMING).

Now a ratamacue has a little more meat to it than a paradiddle and so Walter Thomas was upstairs while I was practicing. And I called him, I said Foots, let's try to make an arrangement on this and call it "Ratamacue" and he sit up there and we did it. Got together with him, he's the one that got it. Now of course with RATAMACUE that beat is a little fast, I did it like this then (DRUMMING). But if it's fast (DRUMMING) . . . it's a bounce the way you do it with the sticks (DRUMMING) . . . And that's how "Ratamacue"
You mentioned you had done that with--
With Stuff and but Walter did a big band arrangement of it, but the same outline as what we had already done.
